stem.en: Same setup — block A was touching B on the other side before the push. What is A's acceleration once B moves away, in m/s²?

explanation.en: Once B separates from A, no force acts on A at all — contact forces only push, they can't pull A along. A's acceleration is exactly 0 m/s², no matter how hard B and C are pushed.

hints.en: Draw A's own free-body diagram once it loses contact with B — how many forces touch A?
A force can only exist where something is actually touching. Is anything still touching A?
